title: Onboarding Lighthouse — UX experiment jottings
content:
Context:
Quick brain dump for a lightweight guided onboarding (codename: Lighthouse) targeted at engineers who sign up and want to validate an LLM integration in <30 minutes. Goal: reduce time-to-first-value while teaching cost/latency tradeoffs and surfaced Redwood best practices (pinning, batching, KV cache hints).

Elevator pitch (one liner):
Lighthouse = a small interactive sandbox + checklist that walks a developer through sample API calls, perf knobs, and a tiny canary rollout so they leave with an actual endpoint, a perf baseline (latency/cost/quality), and a recommended config.

Assumptions / user problems we solve:
- New signups skim docs and copy-paste examples but have no signal about real latency/cost on their prompt shapes.
- People give up if first tests are slow or expensive; they don't know batching/quantization alternatives.
- We can nudge best practices if the onboarding flows surface clear before/after delta metrics.

Core flow (happy path):
1) User lands on Lighthouse from Console or Quickstart link.
2) Short micro-survey: use-case (chat, summarization, embeddings, reranking), expected request sizes, latency sensitivity. Two clicks -> preset.
3) Lighthouse spins up a temporary dedicated route (ephemeral) bound to a sandbox model variant (auto-quantized if supported) for 30 minutes.
4) Guided steps: run sample prompt, see streaming response, toggle batch size / max_tokens / temperature, re-run.
5) Lighthouse shows a small chart: tokens / ms / $ estimate per 1k calls. Shows recommended settings and a single-click export to your account route or to a Dedicated config.
6) Optional: run a simple A/B with a cheaper quantized variant and the base fp32/perf variant to compare latency/cost/quality side-by-side.

Minimum viable pieces to prototype now:
- Tiny UI: micro-survey + single panel sandbox + controls (batch size, max tokens, top_p, quantization toggle).
- Backend: ephemeral route creation OR mock telemetry with recorded perf on standard prompts (cheaper path for prototype).
- Eval harness: lightweight quality comparator (BLEU-ish or human-sim heuristics) to show delta between variants. Start with simple heuristics (token overlap, stop-sequences).
- Cost math: show a simple per-request $ estimate derived from token counts and model unit price.

User stories (rough):
- As a dev, I want a one-click example that returns a response for my prompt so I can validate API connectivity.
- As a developer, I want to compare two model configs to see latency and cost tradeoffs for my prompt so I can pick a sensible default.
- As a PM, I want to capture conversion events (exported route, turned on Dedicated trial) to measure Lighthouse impact on adoption.

Acceptance criteria (for first prototype):
- User can run a prompt and see a real response within 30s of starting Lighthouse.
- Lighthouse displays latency (p95), tokens consumed, and an estimated $/call for the run.
- User can toggle a quantized variant and re-run; the UI shows delta in latency, tokens, and estimated cost.
- Export action persists chosen config as a new route or creates an onboarding note in Console.

Success metrics / KPIs:
- Time to first successful call (target < 3 minutes).
- Conversion: % users who export a route or enable a trial within 24 hours (target +10% vs baseline).
- Deflection: drop in quickstart help tickets related to "slow/expensive" tests.
- Feature usage: fraction of onboarding users who toggle quantization or batching controls at least once (signal that they learned).

Experiment ideas / variants to A/B test:
- Full-ephemeral route vs simulated telemetry (faster but less realistic).
- Frictionless export (single click) vs gated (confirm cost/commitment).
- Include a short checklist (pin model, set batching) vs no checklist.

Open questions / risks:
- Ephemeral route provisioning latency and infra cost for many concurrent signups — need throttles.
- UX: will showing $ estimates early scare developers off? maybe show relative % delta first and a soft $ hint.
- Security: if we let users upload example data, we must ensure it doesn't persist unless they export. GDPR concerns.
- Measuring quality is hard; heuristics may mislead; consider capturing a small manual label set from beta users.

Things to prototype first sprint (2 weeks):
- UI mock + clickthrough (product).
- Backend quick path: use recorded perf on canonical prompts for the chosen preset, plus a pass-through for live calls for power users (engineering).
- Basic cost calculator and export-to-route stub (platform).

Notes to self / design nudges (informal):
- Keep language focused on "test in your environment" not marketing fluff. Engineers appreciate exact numbers.
- Provide one simple recommended config after the comparison ("we recommend: small-quant, batch=8, max_tokens=256") and a link to docs on why.
- Consider a tiny onboarding email sequence that surfaces their Lighthouse baseline and tips after 24 hours.

Next steps (actionable):
- Share this doc with Jordan and Maya for product/eng feasibility call.
- Set up a short spike: mock UI + fake telemetry + single export button. Owner: Riya. Due: 2025-08-28.
- Create a Linear ticket for ephemeral route capacity planning (ONB-412 linked above).

Scratch ideas for later phases:
- Auto-suggest model variant given usage patterns and budget target.
- Lightweight team templates ("support bot", "docs summarizer") that pre-fill checks and prompt sets.
- Micro-credential: after completing Lighthouse, user gets a small badge and a short config snippet they can embed in README.

Random brainlets scribbled here:
- Could embed a tiny recorded session of a senior Redwood engineer running through the flow (video 90s) to reduce cognitive load.
- Make quantization toggle a "try cheaper" CTA with a risk indicator instead of technical jargon.
- Track cohort of Lighthouse users to see long-term retention vs non-Lighthouse cohort.

End of dump.

(If I come back to this later: sketch quick wireframes, map backend spike tasks, and add privacy note for uploads.)
